items.sentence: The MHRA says large studies of millions of children have found no evidence that vaccines cause autism, and reaffirms the safety of childhood vaccination.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA published its statement reaffirming the safety of childhood vaccination on 12 August 2026.

items.sentence: Its Chief Safety Officer, Dr Alison Cave, says large, well-conducted studies of millions of children worldwide consistently show no evidence that vaccines cause autism.

items.sentence: The statement cites a study of 2.56 million US children that found no link between MMR vaccination before age 2 and autism.

items.sentence: The MHRA has published a statement reaffirming the safety of childhood vaccination.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: Dr Alison Cave, the MHRA's Chief Safety Officer, says that multiple large, well-conducted studies involving millions of children worldwide consistently show no evidence that vaccines cause autism.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The notes to the statement cite a study of 2.56 million children in the United States that found no association between MMR vaccination before age 2 and childhood autism.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The statement also points to a recent large study that found no evidence of increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism, from early childhood exposure to aluminium-containing vaccines.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: The MHRA says it monitors vaccine safety continuously through the Yellow Card scheme, analysis of large healthcare datasets, review of international safety data and ongoing review by independent scientific experts.
items.note: Stated in the retrieved search summary of the source page.

items.sentence: Dr Cave encouraged parents to follow NHS vaccination guidance and to speak to a healthcare professional if they have questions.
